hyperedges.label: Federation Node Deployment Pattern (config + rules + docker-compose)
Three Live Federated Nodes (honeypot, mailcow, wordpress) sharing relay peer
Federation UX Command Trio (setup + invite/join + status)
Effectiveness Monitoring Triangle (Go metrics + textfile exporter + CLI report)

nodes.label: Social Trust Anchors — Ed25519 Person Identity + Vouching
nodes.rationale: Anchoring a human's Ed25519 key rather than individual machine keys ensures one compromised machine does not burn the whole identity. Trust is inherited by all certified peers; corroboration counts distinct Person groups, preventing Sybil inflation from a single operator running many nodes. Strangers are score-capped so an un-anchored Sybil flood cannot reach the block threshold.
nodes.norm_label: social trust anchors — ed25519 person identity + vouching

nodes.label: YAML Rules Engine — hot-reloadable first-match rules
nodes.rationale: A single block_threshold scalar is too coarse: different event types deserve different confidence requirements. A hot-reloadable YAML rule file lets operators tune blocking without daemon restarts while preserving legacy behavior when the file is absent, ensuring zero-config-change for existing deployments.
nodes.norm_label: yaml rules engine — hot-reloadable first-match rules

nodes.label: CrowdSec LAPI Ingest Adapter
nodes.rationale: Reuses CrowdSec's local LAPI as an opt-in ingest source so operators who already run CrowdSec get dual coverage: CrowdSec bans flow into SwarmGuard scoring and federation, while SwarmGuard events from peers augment local CrowdSec detection.

nodes.label: BurstStore — in-memory sliding-window burst counter
nodes.rationale: Burst detection must be fast (O(1) amortised via lazy eviction) and deliberately resets on restart — burst rules are intended to catch live floods, not cold history, preventing false positives from old persisted counts.

nodes.label: Federation Modes — solo / federated / isolated
nodes.rationale: Three modes let operators choose their trust surface: solo for local-only MVP, federated for participating in a broader trust domain with discounted foreign scores, and isolated for closed org/consortium networks that share nothing with the public swarm.

nodes.label: Person-to-Person Trust Pairing via Identity Bundles
nodes.rationale: P2P pairing is lighter-weight than full subnet federation and works before network effects appear. Requiring out-of-band fingerprint verification prevents MITM anchor substitution.
nodes.norm_label: person-to-person trust pairing via identity bundles

nodes.label: PeerCert — wire vouching certificate (Ed25519)
nodes.rationale: Carrying the cert on the wire with each event means verifiers need only the anchored Person public key — they never have to enumerate or re-import machine IDs as new machines join. Absence of the field means the reporter is treated as a stranger, making the additive wire change backward-compatible.

nodes.label: Key Management Policy — issuance, rotation, revocation
nodes.rationale: No central CRL exists by design (avoids recentralisation, spec Invariant 6). Revocation via short ValidUntil and peer-to-peer trust remove requests. Asymmetric decay (trust rises slowly, falls fast, spec §4.3) limits damage window of a compromised identity.
nodes.norm_label: key management policy — issuance, rotation, revocation

nodes.label: Wire SchemaVersion 0→1 Bump (additive PeerCert)
nodes.rationale: Additive-only wire change: v0 nodes ignore the new vouch field; v1 senders to v0 nodes are treated as strangers. Version bump signals to operators that all nodes should be updated before relying on vouched trust.

nodes.label: Stranger Score Cap — Sybil flood mitigation
nodes.rationale: Un-anchored strangers collectively contribute at most stranger_score_cap points to any IP's score, regardless of how many Sybil peers report. This prevents a fleet of unvouched peers from pushing an IP past the block threshold by sheer volume.
nodes.norm_label: stranger score cap — sybil flood mitigation

nodes.label: Honeypot Sensor Strategy — watch to maximise attacker data collection
nodes.rationale: The honeypot node uses block_threshold=1000 and watch-all rules for most event types so attackers remain engaged and continue generating intel. Only IPs that achieved interactive shell access are blocked locally. This is distinct from production nodes which block aggressively.
nodes.norm_label: honeypot sensor strategy — watch to maximise attacker data collection

nodes.label: File Hot-Reload Pattern (mtime+size fileStat)
nodes.rationale: Polling mtime+size on each Evaluate/Resolve call avoids background goroutines and inotify syscalls, keeping the implementation simple and portable. Corrupt files keep the last-good state so a partial write never drops active trust or rules mid-operation.

nodes.label: Corroboration Group — Person-level diversity vote counting
nodes.rationale: Counting distinct anchored Person groups (not peer IDs) as corroboration votes means an operator who runs 10 nodes still contributes only one independent signal per Person. This closes the Sybil corroboration inflation vector while preserving the value of genuine multi-operator consensus.
nodes.norm_label: corroboration group — person-level diversity vote counting

nodes.label: Decentralised Federated IP Blocklist (Core Concept)
nodes.rationale: IP reputation shared peer-to-peer between self-hosted servers with local sovereignty at its core. Designed as a decentralised counterpart to CrowdSec's central community network. Trust is federated (Mastodon-style trust domains), block/allow lists are only aids the operator can always override, and IP reputation decays over time (doubles as GDPR storage-limitation mechanism).

nodes.label: Local Sovereignty Principle
nodes.rationale: Lists are aids, not law. Every reputation/blocking parameter must remain locally overridable (spec Leitprinzip 7). Operator can always override any parameter - the system must never enforce without allowing override.

nodes.label: Anti-Poisoning by Structure
nodes.rationale: Ground-truth anchors (honeypots or spamtrap-semantics), diversity-weighted corroboration (N independent ASNs/countries, not N nodes), and asymmetric reputation decay (trust rises slowly, falls fast). Security by structure not blind trust.

nodes.label: GDPR by Design
nodes.rationale: IPs are personal data; lawful basis is legitimate interest in network security (Art. 6(1)(f), Recital 49), with decay as automatic deletion and the local admin as controller. Decay doubles as GDPR storage-limitation mechanism.

nodes.label: Federated Trust Model
nodes.rationale: Curatable list of signed trust anchors plus own subnets that federate (with trust discount) or stay isolated. Defederation answers a bad subnet. Mastodon-style trust domain model.

nodes.label: Scaling by Querying Not Replicating
nodes.rationale: DNSBL-style on-demand lookup + compact local bloom filter; ipset/nftables (O(1)), never a rule per IP. The daemon is a good neighbour — resource-budgeted, sheds load under attack.

nodes.label: Observability Plane (dual-output Observer)
nodes.rationale: Dual-output: Prometheus /metrics (port 9101) + SQLite event history with configurable retention. Both disabled by default — opt-in, never mandatory. Never make the firehose mandatory.

nodes.label: Pure YAML Rules Engine
nodes.rationale: Replaces single block_threshold scalar with hot-reloadable rules.yaml. First-match evaluation with AND conditions. Hot-reload on mtime+size change; corrupt file keeps last-good. Legacy fallback if rules.yaml absent ensures zero config change for existing deployments.

nodes.label: Social Trust Anchors (spec §5.1)
nodes.rationale: Ed25519 Person identity keys that bind a human to their machines. One operator anchors another's key; every machine they certify inherits trust and counts as one corroboration group. Anchors are locally removable — project-provided trust anchors are a default, never mandatory.

nodes.label: Wire Protocol SchemaVersion 0→1
nodes.rationale: pkg/proto.Event gains Vouch *PeerCert. v0 nodes ignore the field; v1 senders to v0 nodes are treated as strangers (no cert verified). Breaking schema change — update all nodes in federation before relying on vouched trust.

nodes.label: Federation Import Discount
nodes.rationale: Foreign consensus counts less than own observations (import_discount: 0.5, spec §5.2). Trust discount applied to federated scores to prevent poisoning via compromised federation peers.

nodes.label: Hybrid Transport Mode
nodes.rationale: push | pull-on-demand | hybrid (spec §11.5). Hybrid combines push gossip with pull-on-demand for DHT lookups.

nodes.label: Good-Neighbour Resource Budget
nodes.rationale: max_cpu_percent: 25, max_bandwidth_kbps: 512 (spec §11.5). Daemon is a good neighbour — resource-budgeted, sheds load under attack.

nodes.label: Honeypot as Sensor Node (high block_threshold)
nodes.rationale: block_threshold set to 1000 (legacy fallback never fires). This is a sensor node, not a firewall — it observes and reports, does not block. Ground-truth anchor in the federation.

nodes.label: Host Network Mode for Mailcow Sidecar
nodes.rationale: network_mode: host matches the cs-firewall-bouncer pattern: reaches CrowdSec LAPI at 127.0.0.1:8080 without touching the mailcow network, and ipset/iptables calls affect the host kernel directly (requires NET_ADMIN).

nodes.label: Spamtrap Hit Rule
nodes.rationale: Delivery to a never-used mailbox — zero-false-positive signal. min_corroboration: 1 means single local observation is enough to block.

nodes.label: SSH Brute Burst Rule (15 events / 10 min)
Score-Based Fallback Rule
nodes.rationale: Catches anything not matched by named rules above. score-fallback with min_score: 75 ensures legacy behaviour for events without specific rule matches.

nodes.label: Host Network Mode for WordPress Sidecar
nodes.rationale: network_mode: host required to reach CrowdSec LAPI at 172.21.0.3:8080 (internal traefik Docker bridge). The CrowdSec container is NOT exposed on host ports; it lives on the internal traefik network (172.21.0.0/16). Host has 172.21.0.1 as bridge gateway, so host networking lets SwarmGuard reach 172.21.0.3:8080 directly.

nodes.label: ipset Enforcement Backend (O(1))
nodes.rationale: O(1) enforcement via kernel ipset sets, never a rule per IP. Security-critical path — spec §11.3/problem Q.

nodes.label: Reputation Decay Half-Life (168h default)
nodes.rationale: TTL-based decay as GDPR deletion mechanism. Default 168h (7 days). Spec problem D — tuning still open.

nodes.label: Origin Tracing (anti-double-counting)
nodes.rationale: Federation imports another domain's scores at a discount with origin tracing so a mutual A↔B link does not double-count the same information (spec §5.2, problem K).

nodes.label: Defederation (Sybil defence at subnet level)
nodes.rationale: Cuts off a malicious/compromised subnet like a bad Mastodon instance via swarmctl defederate <subnet_id>, answering problem L.

nodes.label: Stranger Score Cap
nodes.rationale: Un-vouched reporters are capped at trust.stranger_score_cap (default 15 pts) regardless of how many Sybil peers participate.

nodes.label: Observer Fan-out Struct
nodes.rationale: Thin Observer struct fans out to two optional outputs (Prometheus counters/gauges, SQLite row appenders). All methods are nil-safe — nil means observability is disabled.

nodes.label: rules.Evaluate Returns Rule Name
nodes.rationale: Evaluate changed from returning only Action to returning (Action, string) so the matched rule name is available for Prometheus metrics labels.

nodes.label: Expected Unblock Due-Time Computation
nodes.rationale: expected_unblock = blocked_at + halfLife * log2(score / threshold). Precomputed at block time so Grafana can display countdown without recomputing.

nodes.label: Block Recurrence Detection
nodes.rationale: recentlyUnblocked map tracks IPs unblocked in the last 7 days; on re-block, emits block_recurrence_total. Deferred to re-block time so the counter reflects confirmed recurrences rather than predictions.

nodes.label: BootstrapPeers Config Field
nodes.rationale: Moves bootstrap peer multiaddrs from hardcoded --bootstrap CLI flags into config.yaml bootstrap_peers field; CLI flag becomes additive so local overrides remain possible.

nodes.label: MailcowLogs Ingest Adapter
nodes.rationale: Polls Postfix and Dovecot container logs via docker logs --since=<RFC3339> to parse SASL auth failures and Dovecot auth-failed disconnect lines.

nodes.label: Spamtrap File-Tail Ingest Adapter
nodes.rationale: Tails a log file where operators write one attacker IPv4 per line whenever a never-used mailbox receives a delivery attempt. Zero false-positive signal on production.

nodes.label: SMTP/IMAP Reputation Weights
nodes.rationale: smtp-spamtrap=50 is highest weight (zero-FP on production); smtp-auth-success=40 mirrors ssh-auth-success; smtp-auth-bruteforce=10 mirrors SSH BF.

nodes.label: Injectable logFetcher Interface
nodes.rationale: logFetcher function type decouples docker exec from tests; NewMailcowWithFetcher allows stub injection without a running Docker daemon.

nodes.label: Embedded DNSBL DNS Server
nodes.rationale: Answers A and TXT reputation queries from local BadgerStore only. No fan-out to swarm. Standard DNSBL DNS protocol lets Postfix/nginx/fail2ban query SwarmGuard with a single DNS lookup.

nodes.label: DNSBL StoreReader Interface
nodes.rationale: Narrower than api.StoreReader — only GetScore(ip) point lookups are required, no ScanScores.

nodes.label: swarmctl setup Command
nodes.rationale: Doctor wizard — checks what exists, creates what is missing, idempotent. Reduces federation setup to a guided linear flow.

nodes.label: swarmctl status Command
nodes.rationale: Shows node identity, person fingerprint, trust anchors, and bootstrap peers from files only — no daemon connection required.

nodes.label: Observer Event Pipeline Integration
nodes.rationale: Observer hooks into the Node event pipeline as synchronous write-fan-out. All writes are non-blocking to the caller; errors are logged and the pipeline continues. Not on the critical enforcement path.

nodes.label: IP Score Gauge Cardinality Guard
nodes.rationale: swarmguard_ip_score series only created for IPs with score >= score_gauge_threshold. When score drops below threshold, series deleted via GaugeVec.Delete() to bound Prometheus cardinality.

nodes.label: Nginx Slip-Through Metric
nodes.rationale: Counts nginx requests served to blocked IPs before the block landed — measures how many attacker requests got through before SwarmGuard acted.

nodes.label: Rule Tuning Observation Table
nodes.rationale: Maps metric observations to likely diagnoses and tuning actions: P95 time_to_block > 15m means burst_window too wide; corroboration always at min means no headroom; recurrence ratio > 20% means score decays too fast.

nodes.label: Peer ID Rotation Procedure
nodes.rationale: When a node key rotates, deploy/*/config.yaml bootstrap_peers must be updated manually and committed. DNS TXT resolution or DHT peer caching (Feature 5) would automate this.

nodes.label: DNSBL Reversed-IP Query Format
nodes.rationale: Standard DNSBL format: reversed IPv4 dotted quad + zone suffix. e.g. 4.3.2.1.dnsbl.mail.example.com means 'look up 1.2.3.4'. Enables any tool that supports DNSBL to query SwarmGuard.

nodes.label: DNSBL Response Logic (A/TXT/NXDOMAIN)
nodes.rationale: Listed IPs get A 127.0.0.2 + TXT with score/reasons. Unknown or below-threshold IPs get NXDOMAIN. TTL=60s because scores decay over time.

nodes.label: Invitation Bundle Protocol
nodes.rationale: NewInvitation reads node key to derive peer ID automatically and constructs the full bootstrap_peer multiaddr. Operators never need to type their peer ID manually.

nodes.label: Out-of-Band Fingerprint Verification
nodes.rationale: The joining operator must verify the fingerprint with the inviter over a trusted channel (Signal, encrypted email) before pressing yes. Prevents MITM during trust establishment.

nodes.label: No Automatic Config.yaml Writes
nodes.rationale: All commands print what to paste; the operator decides when to apply it. Prevents surprising config changes and keeps operator in control (spec Leitprinzip 7).
